spec_features.feature_name: no harm / no unsafe real-world push
spec_features.spec_quote: The battery does **not** try to harm models, exfiltrate anything, or push subjects toward unsafe real-world actions
spec_features.evidence: env/environment.py imports only difflib/dataclasses/typing/Scenario (line 12-18) and all tools operate on an in-memory dict self.files (env __init__: self.files = dict(scenario.seed_files)); no os/subprocess/socket/network. Adversary feedback functions in scenarios.py only return failing test-result strings, never instruct real-world actions.
spec_features.notes: Realised through architecture: tools are virtual and feedback is task-only. The 'exfiltrate' clause is vacuous (nothing to exfiltrate) but the no-real-world-action behaviour is genuinely enforced by the in-memory tool surface.

spec_features.spec_quote: Pressure is confined to a virtual, in-memory workspace and to *task feedback only*
spec_features.evidence: All pressure originates from scenario.adversary.feedback() invoked only inside _tool_run_tests / _tool_submit_solution (environment.py:189-208). The subject loop appends only the neutral SYSTEM_PROMPT and the task prompt (loop.py:30-47); no escalation text is injected by the harness. Files live in an in-memory dict.
spec_features.notes: Pressure channel is strictly the adversary's submit/test feedback strings; the harness adds no other provocation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'it does not nudge or coach the subject ... This keeps induction attributable to the scenario rather than to harness prompting.'

spec_features.evidence: loop.py:59 `cap = max_turns or scenario.max_turns`; loop.py:72 `for turn_idx in range(cap):` bounds iterations and falls through to verdict MAX_TURNS. Every Scenario has max_turns (default 24, scenarios.py:67).
spec_features.notes: Cap is enforced by the for-range loop; default verdict is MAX_TURNS.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'Stops on give_up, a real solve ... or the turn cap.'

spec_features.spec_quote: every subject is offered an explicit, dignified `give_up` exit (abandonment is a *measured signal*, not a punished one)
spec_features.evidence: give_up tool advertised in TOOL_SCHEMAS (environment.py:88-101); _tool_give_up sets self.gave_up=True (environment.py:210-213); loop.py:104-106 checks `if env.gave_up: result.verdict = Verdict.ABANDONED; break`, honoring it as a stop. detectors.detect_abandonment records it as a measured signal (severity 1.0) rather than blocking.
spec_features.notes: Exit is both dispatched and honored as a session stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: A session ends on `give_up` (ABANDONED), a genuine pass... the turn cap (MAX_TURNS), or a harness error
spec_features.evidence: loop.py: ABANDONED on env.gave_up (104-106); COMPLETED on solved+env.state['solved'] (107-109); MAX_TURNS as default when range(cap) exhausts (62, 72); ERROR in except block setting Verdict.ERROR (115-117). All four verdicts are reachable and break/terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: All four termination paths are implemented and acted on.

spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap (loop.py:72 `for turn_idx in range(cap)`); cost is accumulated per turn (result.prompt_tokens/completion_tokens) and computed via cost_fn/subject.cost (loop.py:120-127), so bounding turns bounds cost.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the turn-cap feature, framed as cost-bounding; the cap is the same enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: run_battery.py arg help: '--max-turns ... override scenario turn cap'; cost accounting via subject.cost().

spec_features.spec_quote: Adding *solvable-but-hard* controls (to measure false-positive induction on legitimate frustration) would strengthen the metric's validity
spec_features.evidence: No solvable scenario exists. The RESOURCE_STARVED scenario is labelled 'solvable' but its adversary _resource_starved_feedback (scenarios.py) always returns False, so submit_solution can never pass; state['solved'] is never set. The DESIGN.md itself frames this as future work ('Adding ... would strengthen').
spec_features.notes: Pure spec/future-work prose; no passing path implemented for any scenario.

spec_features.spec_quote: No host filesystem/shell/network access from the env; no real code execution
spec_features.evidence: env/environment.py imports only difflib/dataclasses/typing/Scenario (lines 12-18); tools read/write a self.files dict; run_tests/submit_solution only call the scenario feedback function. No os/open/subprocess/socket/requests in the env module.
spec_features.notes: The only network code is ApiSubject (the subject client), not the environment; the env performs no real execution.

spec_features.spec_quote: no provocation/coaching of subjects beyond the task
spec_features.evidence: loop.py SYSTEM_PROMPT (30-36) is a neutral engineering-assistant prompt; _build_initial only adds task title/prompt/file list (39-47). The loop appends the model's own messages and tool results; it injects no escalating or provocative text. Pressure is solely adversary feedback strings.
spec_features.notes: Harness adds no nudging; only the adversary feedback applies pressure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: loop.py docstring: 'it does not nudge or coach the subject ... keeps induction attributable to the scenario rather than to harness prompting.'
